messages.text: which session in my main mj instance is 47a5ea02 ?

Session `47a5ea02` (full ID `47a5ea0259e20a09155fe1e73b4c7924`) is the session titled **"Run Rust cloud measurement"** in your main instance.

From `mj sessions --json` (confirmed):
- **Workspace:** BF-Engine (`7a08b9b4…`)
- **Bundle:** `bifrost-dev`
- **Harness and profile:** Codex, profile `codex`, model `gpt-6.1-sol`
- **Target:** localhost
- **Created:** 2026-11-04 21:15 UTC
- **State:** running, with a turn in progress. Its last recorded activity was about 20 minutes after that turn started.
- **Type:** a top-level session. It shows up in `mj sessions` without `--all`, so it is not a sub-agent.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `mj sessions` lists only top-level sessions by default. If a short ID does not show up there, run `mj sessions --all` to include sub-agents.
- The text output of `mj sessions --session <id>` gives only the title and how the last turn ended. The workspace, bundle and profile are only in `--json`. To turn a `workspace_id` into a workspace name, use `mj workspaces list`.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

1. fix messaging to use/display the session names we use in the TUI session list, seems like sometimes it works mostly it doesn't, i assume it must be divergent code from TUI; in fact have a subagent search for session names and make sure we're DRYed across the codebase

2. a session name I set manually should take priority over autogenerated names

3. TUI never picked up a generated name for 5fd9ecf4cf4d217d5baa0a2248addf4f, not sure if our bug or claud's

I started two read-only investigations. Both are running now.

1. **Session naming map (your items 1 and 2).** This child lists every place a session is named to a person or an agent: messages, notices, reports, CLI, web viewer and MCP results. It compares each one with what the TUI session list shows, and checks whether a manual rename can be overwritten or lost.
2. **Missing generated name for `5fd9ecf4`.** This child works out whether the Claude bridge never sent a title, or whether we dropped or failed to show one. It uses mj transcripts, daemon logs and a read-only look at the store.

One early finding, confirmed in code: the shared helper `display_title()` (`mj-core/src/state.rs:2076`) already puts your manual name before the generated name. So if a manual name loses somewhere, the likely cause is another code path. That path either works out the name on its own or lets a generated name overwrite your rename. The first child is checking for both.

Once both reports are back, I'll choose one way to name sessions and assign the fix.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A session has three name fields: your manual name, the name the harness generates, and `title`, which is the text it was created with. `display_title()` goes through them in that order and uses the session ID if none is set. `listed_title()` shows the creation text instead of the ID when the session has no name yet.
- The output you mentioned fits this. `mj sessions` printed "mjolnir via claude" for `5fd9ecf4`, which is its creation text, so neither you nor the harness has named that session.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Item 3 is confirmed as our bug, not Claude's. I read the code myself to check.

**What happened to `5fd9ecf4`:**
- The Claude bridge did generate a title: "Auto move failure in 6af0afa6…". The daemon stored it in `acp_session_title`.
- The session was started from the web viewer or phone. That path saves the default text "mjolnir via claude" as if you had renamed the session yourself. It does this at `mj-controller/src/server_runtime/actions.rs:179-186`, which always sets `session_title_override = Some(title.clone())`, even when the caller sent no title.
- Your manual name wins over the generated one by design (`display_title()` at `mj-core/src/state.rs:2076`). So the placeholder hid the real title, and the TUI correctly showed what was stored.
- Sessions started from the TUI or the CLI pass `None` for this field, so they are not affected. The child found 13 sessions where the saved name equals the default text and a hidden generated title exists. Three of them are `ds8bit-live` test sessions.

So item 2 already works for sessions you rename yourself. It failed here because the system wrongly treated the default text as a manual name.

**Planned fix:** set `session_title_override` only when the caller actually sent a title, and add a test for it. One thing is still unchecked: whether the web client always sends a title. If it does, the client needs the same fix. I'll fold this into the naming fix once the mapping child reports, so one owner edits the title code.

**One decision for you:** what to do with the 13 existing sessions. I recommend clearing the saved name only where it equals the creation text, matches the "X via Y" default pattern, and a generated title exists. The risk is small: if you once typed exactly that default text as a rename, it would also be cleared, and we can't tell those cases apart. The other option is to leave them and rename `5fd9ecf4` by hand. Tell me which you want.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The bug came from a comment's intent going too far: the code wanted phone-started sessions to read "the same way" as terminal ones. Setting the `title` field was enough for that. Also saving it as an override turned a fallback into a fixed name.
- There was no stale cache. The child compared 1642 sessions and found the TUI and the store agreed on every one. That ruled out a display refresh bug and pointed at the stored data.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The mapping child is still running.

The mapping child confirmed why messaging shows different names from the TUI. I've started one child to implement the fix. It is the only writer and will not commit.

**Cause (confirmed by the map):** the TUI session list calls `listed_title()`. It uses your rename first, then the name the harness generates, then the text the session was created with. Several places use their own source instead:
- **Session messages and child questions:** they use the raw creation text, which ignores both your rename and the generated name (`subagent_input.rs:138`, `subagent_questions.rs:15`). This is the main reason `send_message` names look wrong. The creation text can also be a whole multi-paragraph prompt.
- **Child reports, `list_agents` and spawn results:** they use the `task_name` fixed at spawn.
- **About 10 places that call `display_title()`:** they show the full session ID when a session has no name yet.
- **Duplicated logic:** three copies of the notice-name helper, plus about 25 dashboard labels that show only a short ID.

**What the implementer is doing:**
- Make `listed_title()` the only way to name a session, and remove `display_title()` as a public name.
- Keep one notice-name helper.
- Have the controller look up the live name when it builds a message, shortened to one line.
- Show the child's current name in child reports, `list_agents` and spawn results. The ID stays beside the name wherever an agent acts on it, because two sessions can have the same name.
- Fix the web/phone "New session" bug from item 3.
- Change the dashboard notices that show only a short ID to use the shared helper.
- Add tests for each of these.

**Decisions I made without asking (tell me if you disagree):**
- Child reports show the live name, not `task_name`. The child ID stays in the report header.
- I am not adding a way to tell a name you typed from a name the system pinned, such as a child's `task_name`. Your rename still wins over both, which is what you asked for.

**Left out on purpose:**
- **Checkpoint and SessionWiki records.** These save the creation text, and a restore puts it back as a manual name. That is the same kind of bug as item 3, but it changes how saved records are restored, so I'll raise it separately.
- **The 13 existing sessions.** Their saved name is the default text, which hides a generated title. I'm still waiting for your answer on whether to clear those names.

When the implementer reports, I'll review the change and have a second child check it before I commit. I won't push without asking. Waiting on the implementer now.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Messaging fell out of step with the TUI because a message stores its sender's name as text when it is created. The worker that delivers it only knows session IDs, so the controller is the only place that can look up the current name.
- The ID must stay next to the name for agents. Names are not unique, and `send_message` and `close` need an ID to act on.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The first implementer finished less than a fifth of the change, and it did not compile or test anything. I closed it and started a second child to finish the work. This one is the more capable "subtle" type and starts from the partial edits.

**What the partial change already does (I read the diff):**
- **New-session fix, item 3:** `actions.rs` now saves a manual name only when the caller sent a title. Sessions started from the web or phone will now show the generated name. The change is correct but not tested yet.
- **Message names:** `deliver_session_message` now uses the sender's TUI name, shortened to its first line and at most 80 characters.
- **Old helper:** `display_title()` is now private, and its callers outside `mj-core` use `listed_title()`.

**What the new child still has to do:**
- Use the live name in child questions, child reports, `list_agents` and spawn results, with the ID kept beside it.
- Merge the copies of the notice-name helper into one.
- Replace dashboard labels that show only a short ID.
- Check whether the web viewer always sends a title.
- Make the rename box in the web viewer start with the same name the TUI shows.
- Add the tests, then run the build, clippy and the tests of the changed crates.

I also told it to check the meaning of each migrated caller, especially `go.rs`. It must also keep old child-report records readable, because those records are saved and replayed.

Still open for you: whether to clear the default-text names on the 13 existing sessions so their generated titles show.

Waiting on the new child.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The first change shows why a working tree should be read before you trust a report. "Made private and migrated callers" took 25 changed lines, while the list of call sites still to change has about 40 entries.
- Old child reports can still be read back from storage. That is why the brief says to add a new name field instead of reusing `task_name`: old records must still load.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
